newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA BULLION TRADE SHUT IN BOMBAY FOR TAX PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: INDIA BULLION TRADE SHUT IN BOMBAY FOR TAX PROTEST.

text.p: The Bombay Bullion market shut down on Tuesday as dealers and dealers and jewellers held a one-day strike to protest against raids and harassment by income tax department in the bullion market.
"Income tax officals have raided leading local bullion dealers last week and search was going on since Friday," said M. Damani, president of Bombay Bullion Association.
"Today's strike is a token strike for one day," he said.
"We have also represented this issue to the state government."
On Monday gold 24 carat was steady at 4,495 rupees per 10 gramme while prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) were steady at 52,600 rupees per piece.
Silver (.999) was up by 25 rupees at 6,350 rupees per kg on Monday. During last week silver was down by 45 rupees per kg while prices of a gold biscuit were down by 400 rupees per piece.
